anchor.rationale: The baseline is the schema AT the first commit that created the database file the product actually opens (woclaw.sqlite). A database created before that file name existed is a DIFFERENT file and can never be opened by the current product, so it can never be a migration target. The anchor is deliberately NOT diff-based and NOT per-table-first-appearance: 8a4ebb4 deleted the SQLite storage and 0ebf137 re-added it under the new file name, so a diff-based anchor finds the RE-ADDITION for one table and the ORIGINAL for another, and a first-appearance anchor would demand ALTER arms for columns every real database already has.

note: Columns present in each table's CREATE TABLE as of the anchor commit (or at the table's own introducing commit, for tables added later). Derived once from git history (`python3 r516_schema_drift_gate.py --derive-baseline`). A column in the current CREATE TABLE that is in neither this baseline nor an ALTER TABLE is a migration gap: it will not exist in databases created before it was added.
